messages.text: The catering company just called. They can't deliver to the conference hall on Friday because the loading dock will be closed for repairs.
That's a setback. Could they use the side entrance on Elm Street instead?
I asked. The carts are too wide for that door, but they offered to bring everything in smaller trays if we push lunch back thirty minutes.
That works. The keynote can run a little longer. I'll let the speaker know and revise the printed agenda.
Great. I'll confirm with the caterer and ask facilities to keep the side door unlocked from noon.

questions.stem: What problem does Ms. Nair report?
options: A. The caterer has canceled the order.
B. A delivery area will be unavailable.
C. The keynote speaker will arrive late.
D. The conference hall has been double-booked.
questions.explanation: Ms. Nair says the caterer cannot deliver because 'the loading dock will be closed for repairs.'

questions.stem: At 2:16 P.M., why does Mr. Whitaker write, "The keynote can run a little longer"?
options: A. To complain that the speaker talks too much
B. To suggest canceling the lunch break
C. To show that the schedule can absorb the delay
D. To ask Ms. Nair to contact the speaker
questions.explanation: Lunch must be pushed back thirty minutes. By extending the keynote, Mr. Whitaker shows the delay can be filled without leaving a gap in the program. He says he will contact the speaker himself.

questions.stem: The word "revise" in Mr. Whitaker's message at 2:16 P.M. is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Mr. Whitaker will change the printed agenda to reflect the new lunch time, so 'revise' means 'update.' 'Review' only means to look over, without changing.
